Every person reached by at least one channel buys 4 times per year at 45 dollars per purchase, regardless of how many channels reach them. Nobody else buys. The shares are exact and sales tax is excluded. What is total annual spending by unique buyers, in millions of dollars?
instances.spoken_text: A consumer business combines two overlapping customer lists. The population is two million people. Channel A reaches sixty percent of the population, channel B reaches twenty percent, and exactly twenty percent of the entire population is reached by both. Every person reached by at least one channel buys four times per year at forty-five dollars per purchase, regardless of how many channels reach them. Nobody else buys. The shares are exact and sales tax is excluded. What is total annual spending by unique buyers, in millions of dollars?

follow_up.question: What changes if the channel overlap is unknown?
follow_up.reference: The unique-buyer count is no longer determined by the two channel shares alone. You would need an overlap estimate or a defensible range before claiming one exact market size.
